extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, and courts (users of early U.S. patent statute and precedent)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and remedies set out by the U.S. Patent Act of February 21, 1793 (and accompanying judicial interpretations) for obtaining, describing, assigning, challenging, and enforcing patents — including novelty, specification/enablement, procedure, fees, and infringement remedies. Useful for drafting, prosecuting, and litigating patents under that law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: When any person... shall allege that he or they have invented any new and useful art, machine, manufacture or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement on any art, machine, manufacture or composition of matter, not known or used before the application
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute requires novelty ("not known or used before the application") and utility ("new and useful"). Includes improvements on existing arts/machines/compositions provided they are not previously known or used. Case law interprets novelty as relative to the public ("not known or used by the public before the application") and requires originality as to the whole world (not merely within the U.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, contents, and term of letters patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters patent... reciting the allegations and suggestions of the said petition, and giving a short description of the said invention or discovery, and thereupon granting... for a term not exceeding fourteen years, the full and exclusive right and liberty of making, constructing, using, and vending...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent must state petitioner’s allegations and a short description; the statutory maximum term is 14 years. Letters to be issued in the name of the United States and recorded in Secretary of State's office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-issuance examination by Attorney General
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters patent shall be delivered to the Attorney General, to be examined; who, within fifteen days after such delivery, if he finds the same conformable to this act, shall certify accordingly...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorney General review within 15 days required; AG certifies conformity before Secretary of State executes and seals patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or affirmation of inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Every inventor, before he can receive a patent, shall swear or affirm, that he does verily believe, that he is the true inventor or discoverer of the art, machine, or improvement, for which he solicits a patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath to be made before an authorized officer and delivered with application. Judicially treated as a prerequisite to granting but not essential to validity if omitted inadvertently (courts have held the patent may still be valid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification / written description and enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: Shall deliver a written description of his invention, and of the manner of using, or process of compounding the same, in such full, clear and exact terms, as to distinguish the same from all other things before known, and to enable any person skilled in the art or science... to make, compound, and use the same
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification must (1) distinguish the invention from prior art, (2) enable a person skilled in the art to make and use it, and (3) be full, clear and exact. For machines the principle and several contemplated modes must be explained. Signed by inventor and attested by two witnesses; certified copies admissible in court. Courts will void patents for ambiguous descriptions or concealment intended to deceive, but may permit reissue where defects arose from inadvertence without fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings, specimens, and models where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: He shall accompany the whole with drawings and written references, where the nature of the case admits of drawings, or with specimens of the ingredients, and of the composition of matter, sufficient in quantity for the purpose of experiment... And such inventor shall, moreover, deliver a model of his machine, provided, the secretary shall deem such model to be necessary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where practicable drafts and specimens must be provided; models are required at Secretary's discretion. Drawings and specimens support enablement and the court-admissibility of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing and attestation of specification; filing and evidentiary effect
rubrics_metrics.description: This description, signed by himself and attested by two witnesses, shall be filed in the office of the Secretary of State, and certified copies thereof shall be competent evidence, in all courts, where any matter or thing, touching such patent-right, shall come in question
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification must be signed and witnessed and filed; certified copies serve as competent court evidence in patent disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and limits of improvement patents
rubrics_metrics.description: That any person, who shall have discovered an improvement... and shall have obtained a patent for such improvement, he shall not be at liberty to make, use or vend the original discovery, nor shall the first inventor be at liberty to use the improvement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute contemplates mutual exclusivity between original invention and patented improvements. Judicially, where patent claims an improvement, patent protection should normally be limited to that improvement and not improperly extend to the whole prior machine; if a patent improperly claims the whole, it may be void to the extent it covers more than the inventor’s contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes of form or proportion not constituting discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Simply changing the form or the proportions of any machine, or composition of matter, in any degree, shall not be deemed a discovery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor cosmetic or proportional alterations do not qualify as patentable discoveries; emphasizes substantive novelty over trivial modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and recording; assignee stands in inventor’s place
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be lawful for any inventor, his executor or administrator to assign the title and interest... and the assignee having recorded the said assignment, in the office of the Secretary of State, shall thereafter stand in the place of the original inventor, both as to right and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments should be recorded in Secretary of State's office to perfect rights; recording makes assignee successor in rights and responsibilities and affects standing to sue/defend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for unauthorized making/using/selling (penalty/treble)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person shall make, devise and use, or sell the thing so invented... without the consent of the patentee... every person so offending, shall forfeit and pay to the patentee, a sum, that shall be at least equal to three times the price, for which the patentee has usually sold or licensed to other persons, the use of the said invention; which may be recovered in an action on the case
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute prescribes at least treble monetary penalty based on usual sale/license price; enforceable by action in circuit or other competent courts. Case law explains trebling procedure: jury finds single damages; court trebles them; treble may be applied to profits received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant’s permitted defenses and notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant... shall be permitted to plead the general issue, and give this act and any special matter, of which notice in writing may have been given to the plaintiff or his attorney, thirty days before trial, in evidence, tending to prove, that the specification... does not contain the whole truth... or that the thing, thus secured by patent, was not originally discovered by the patentee, but had been in use, or had been described in some public work anterior to the supposed discovery...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant may plead general issue and present prior use/publication, insufficiency, fraud, or that the patentee is not the original inventor as defenses; must give 30 days’ written notice of special matter before trial; if proven, judgment for defendant and patent void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interfering applications — arbitration procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of interfering applications, the same shall be submitted to the arbitration of three persons, one of whom shall be chosen by each of the applicants, and the third person shall be appointed by the Secretary of State; and the decision or award of such arbitrators... shall be final, as far as respects the granting of the patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where two or more applicants conflict over the same invention, arbitration by three arbitrators (each applicant picks one; Secretary picks third) resolves who receives the patent; Secretary may appoint arbitrators if applicants fail to agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging surreptitious or fraudulently obtained patents (time limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon oath or affirmation... that any patent... was obtained surreptitiously, or upon false suggestion, and motion made... within three years after issuing the said patent, but not afterwards, it shall and may be lawful for the judge... to grant a rule, that the patentee... show cause why process should not issue against him to repeal such patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party may move within three years after issue to have a district judge review claims a patent was surreptitiously or fraudulently obtained; if judge finds insufficient cause, judgment may be rendered to repeal patent. The three-year limit is jurisdictional for such motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-granted preexisting exclusive rights and relinquishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any state... shall have granted an exclusive right to any invention, the party, claiming that right, shall not be capable of obtaining an exclusive right under this act, but on relinquishing his right under such particular state
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties holding prior state-granted exclusive rights must relinquish those state rights to obtain a federal patent under this Act; relinquishment followed by obtaining federal right is sufficient evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending prior-law applications treated under new act
rubrics_metrics.description: The persons, whose applications for patents, were... depending before the Secretary of State, Secretary at War, and Attorney General... on complying with the conditions of this act, and paying the fees herein required, may pursue their respective claims to a patent under the same
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications pending under the earlier (1790) law may be prosecuted under the 1793 Act if applicants comply with its conditions and pay required fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and pre-application payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every inventor, before he presents his petition to the Secretary of State... shall pay into the treasury thirty dollars, for which he shall take duplicate receipts... and the money, thus paid, shall be in full for the sundry services, to be performed in the office of the Secretary of State
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must pay $30 before petitioning (statutory fee for office services); copying fees specified: 20 cents per 100-word copy-sheet; $2 per drawing copy; payments accounted as clerk-hire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of prior act without invalidating existing patents (proviso)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the act... of April 10, 1790... be, and the same is hereby repealed. Provided... that nothing, contained in this act, shall be construed to invalidate any patent, that may have been granted under the authority of the said act
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1790 Act repealed but existing patents issued under it remain valid and patentees retain statutory protections for subsequent violations committed after passage of the 1793 Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification concealment or addition as ground for invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: That the defendant... may give in evidence... that the specification, filed by the plaintiff, does not contain the whole truth relative to his discovery, or that it contains more than is necessary to produce the described effect, which concealment or addition shall fully appear to have been made, for the purpose of deceiving the public...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concealment of material facts or addition beyond necessity aimed to deceive public is ground for declaring patent void. Courts distinguish inadvertent mistakes (may allow surrender/reissue) from intentional deception (void).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to distinguish improvement from prior art and confine patent to new parts
rubrics_metrics.description: If it be for an improvement in an existing machine, he must, in his patent, distinguish the new from the old; and confine his patent to such parts only as are new; for if both are mixed up together, and a patent is taken out for the whole, it is void
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent drafter must clearly identify and limit claims to the inventor's contribution; claiming the whole machine when only an improvement was invented risks invalidation for overclaiming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original inventor requirement (priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a patent under the laws of the United States, the party must be the original inventor in reference to the whole world; it is not sufficient that he is the first inventor within the United States
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority requires being original inventor globally; a subsequent inventor cannot obtain a valid patent if the first original inventor perfected and put the invention into actual use, even if that use was secret or limited in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment/dedication to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: It has not, and it cannot be denied, that an inventor may abandon his invention, and surrender or dedicate it to the public. The inchoate right thus given, cannot afterwards be resumed at his pleasure... The true meaning of the words... 'not known or used before the application,' is, not known or used by the public, before the application
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inventor voluntarily allows the invention to become public (use by others, public dedication), his right may be abandoned and he cannot later claim patent rights. Public notice of invention can preserve rights by showing intent to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent cannot be for an effect only; must claim manner/means
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent can in no case be for an effect only, but for an effect produced in a certain manner, or by a peculiar operation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims directed purely to results without specifying how the result is produced are insufficient; invention must be defined by the method or structure producing the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of patents — fair and liberal
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents and the specifications annexed thereto, should be construed fairly and liberally, and not be subject to any over nice or critical refinements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should interpret patents reasonably and not apply excessively narrow or pedantic constructions; nevertheless specification must be sufficiently definite to inform the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of combination distinct from novelty of ingredients
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary to the validity of a patent for a new and useful invention, that any of the ingredients should be new and unused before for the purpose. The true question is, whether the combination of materials by the patentee, is substantially new
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combination patents may be valid even if individual components are known, provided the overall combination is substantially new and produces a new result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of infringement for combination patents vs separate machines
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be for a new combination of machines to produce certain effects... in such a case, the patent being for the combination only, it is no infringement of the patent to use any of the machines separately, if the whole combination be not used
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement of a combination patent requires use of the claimed combination as a whole; using only parts not covered by combination claim may not infringe. Conversely, if patent claims several distinct improvements in aggregate, using any one improvement may infringe depending on claim language and judicial interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages principles — actual, nominal, trebling, counsel fees
rubrics_metrics.description: By the provisions... the law gives to a plaintiff treble the actual damages sustained by him... By the term 'actual damage,' which the plaintiff may recover under the patent law, is meant such damages as he can actually prove... If there be a mere making, and no use proved, nominal damages, are to be recovered... The jury are to find single damages, and the court are to treble them... The jury may... give the plaintiff, as a part of his actual damages, such expenses for counsel fees, &c., as have been actually incurred in vindicating his right by suit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiff recovers provable actual damages (value of use during proven period); if only making and no use, nominal damages. Jury finds single damages; court trebles. Courts may include counsel fees actually incurred as part of recoverable actual damages in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction practice for patent suits — affidavit/inventor status sworn
rubrics_metrics.description: On an application for an injunction to restrain the infringement of a patent right, it should be stated in the bill, or by affidavit, that the complainant is the inventor, and the bill must be sworn to: it is not sufficient that this fact was sworn to when the patent was obtained
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain an injunction the plaintiff must aver and swear in the bill or affidavit that he is the inventor; prior oath at patent issuance is insufficient for the injunction motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings to repeal patents — scire facias and pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: The proceedings under the 10th section of the act of 1793, are in the nature of a scire facias at common law, to repeal a patent... The scire facias in such a case ought to contain a direct allegation or suggestion that the patent was obtained surreptitiously or upon false suggestion; and to call upon the defendant for that cause only, to show cause why the patent should not be repealed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule-to-show-cause proceedings should mirror scire facias; pleadings must allege surreptitious obtaining or false suggestion directly and seek only repeal on those grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence rules and presumptions in patent litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is no objection to the competency of a witness in a patent cause that he is sued in another action for the infringement of the patent... There is a presumption of law, that where a patent and the specifications and drawings have been recorded in the patent office, every person who takes out a patent for a similar machine has a knowledge of the preceding patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts permit witnesses even if parties to related suits. Recording a patent creates a presumption of public knowledge of that patent for subsequent applicants; defendants may rely on many grounds of defense beyond those enumerated in Section 6 (e.g., alienage, license, nonperformance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender and reissue for defective patents (executive correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a defect in the specification on which a patent has issued, arose from inadvertence or mistake, and without any fraud or misconduct on the part of the patentee, the Secretary of State has authority to accept a surrender of the patent, and cancel the record thereof; whereupon he may issue a new patent on an amended specification for the unexpired fourteen years granted by the first patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary of State may accept surrender and reissue a corrected patent for remaining term when defect arose from inadvertence (not fraud); reissued patent relates back to the original patent's date for term purposes.
